Binds the listing cache to the event store’s directory, loading any cache already written there for this zone. Called by the ensemble before priming.
title: setLocalStoreDirectory(_:discardingExistingCache:)
rawIndexableTextContent: Binds the listing cache to the event store’s directory, loading any cache already written there for this zone. Called by the ensemble before priming.  Discussion Rebinding to a different directory drops the in-memory listing and token: they describe the previous store and must not leak across. With discardingExistingCache, any cache file already in the directory is deleted instead of loaded. The ensemble passes this when the store is being rebuilt. The deletion is explicit rather than relying on the rebuilt directory happening to be empty: whether a cache file is present at that moment depends on the order in which the event store removes and recreates its directory, and this guarantee is too important to rest on another type’s internal sequencing.

rawIndexableTextContent: A CloudKit-backed cloud file system.  Overview Stores files as CKRecord objects with CKAsset attachments. Supports custom zones, server change token caching for efficient incremental fetches, and CKShare-based sharing. Preserves exact CKRecord type names (CDEFileSystemNode, CDEItem) and field names from the original Objective-C implementation for backwards compatibility. Setup Enable the iCloud capability in your Xcode project Check CloudKit under iCloud services Create or select a CloudKit container (e.g. iCloud.com.yourcompany.yourapp) Initialize the file system:  No API keys or OAuth tokens are needed — CloudKit uses the device’s iCloud account automatically. Schema Versions CloudKitSchemaVersion.v1 — Original schema with separate CDEDataFile records. Use this for backward compatibility with existing Ensembles 2 CloudKit data. CloudKitSchemaVersion.v2 — Simplified schema without CDEDataFile records. Recommended for new apps. Database Scope Use usePublicDatabase: false (private database) for most apps. The private database syncs across the user’s own devices via their iCloud account. The public database is shared across all users and requires no iCloud sign-in, but has different quota limits. Zone Lifetime An instance is bound to the CloudKit zone incarnation it was primed against: its cached listing and server change token describe that zone’s history and no other. If the zone is deleted or recreated outside the framework — in the CloudKit Console, with your own CloudKit code, or by the user removing the app’s iCloud data in Settings — discard the instance and create a fresh one, and treat the deletion as a full cloud reset: detach and re-attach every device that ever synced with the zone. Prefer CoreDataEnsemble.removeEnsemble(withIdentifier:in:) for resets you control; it deletes records through the framework, so all local caches follow along and the zone itself is never destroyed. Migrating from Ensembles 2 The two private-database initializers write to different CloudKit zones: init(ubiquityContainerIdentifier:rootDirectory:usePublicDatabase:schemaVersion:) uses CloudKit’s default zone (_defaultZone). init(privateDatabaseForUbiquityContainerIdentifier:schemaVersion:) uses a custom zone named com.mentalfaculty.ensembles.zone.schema2. E2 had the same two initializers with the same zone behaviour. If you are migrating an existing E2 fleet to E3 and some users may still be running E2 during the rollout, use the same initializer in E3 that your E2 build used. Devices in different zones cannot see each other’s records, even when pointing at the same iCloud container with the same schema version. Switch to the recommended custom-zone form only after your fleet has fully migrated. Publishing the Schema CloudKit schemas must be deployed to production before your app ships. After testing in the Development environment: Open CloudKit Console Select your container Go to Deploy Schema to Production Review the record types and deploy The schema is created automatically in Development when you first run the app, but it won’t be visible to production users until you deploy it. Sharing For CKShare-based sharing with a custom zone:

rawIndexableTextContent: A CloudKit-based cloud backend for Ensembles. Overview EnsemblesCloudKit provides CloudKitFileSystem, an implementation of the Ensembles CloudFileSystem protocol that stores sync data in iCloud using CloudKit. It handles file upload, download, and directory management through CloudKit record operations. CloudKit is the recommended backend for most apps — it requires no server setup, no authentication UI, and syncs automatically across all of a user’s iCloud devices. Xcode Setup Open your Xcode project and select the app target. Go to Signing & Capabilities and click + Capability. Add iCloud. Check CloudKit under iCloud services. Create or select a CloudKit container (e.g., iCloud.com.yourcompany.yourapp). The container identifier must be unique across all apps. Quick Start  Or use the container for a simpler setup:  Database Scope CloudKit offers three database scopes: Private database (default) — Syncs across the current user’s own iCloud devices. Data is only accessible to the signed-in iCloud account. This is the recommended scope for most apps. Public database — Data is accessible to all users of the app, even without iCloud sign-in. Uses different quota limits (per-app rather than per-user). Useful for shared reference data. Shared database — Used with CKShare for sharing specific data between users.  Schema Versions CloudKit uses record types to store sync data. Two schema versions are available: .v1 — The original schema with three record types: CDEFileSystemNode, CDEItem, and CDEDataFile. Use this when continuing an existing Ensembles 2 deployment that was on schema 1. .v2 — A simplified schema that removes the CDEDataFile record type. Slightly more efficient. Use this for new apps and for E2 fleets that were already on schema 2. There is no implicit default — every initializer requires an explicit schemaVersion. For new apps, use .v2. Publishing Schema to Production You must deploy the CloudKit schema to production before submitting your app to the App Store. Without this step, the app will fail to sync for end users. In the development environment, CloudKit creates record types automatically on first use. Before submitting to the App Store: Run your app at least once in the development environment so that CloudKit creates the necessary record types. Open CloudKit Console. Select your container. Go to Schema → Deploy to Production. Review and deploy. The production schema cannot be modified once deployed (only extended with new fields), so test thoroughly in development first. Sharing with CKShare For apps that share data between users via CKShare:  Implement CloudKitFileSystemDelegate to handle share setup and participant management. Data Security Ensembles stores all sync data as CKAsset binary files attached to CloudKit records — not as structured record fields. The contents are opaque serialized event logs that are not human-readable, even without encryption. CloudKit encrypts all data at rest on Apple’s servers. With Advanced Data Protection (ADP) enabled, CKAsset data is end-to-end encrypted — Apple cannot read it. Without ADP, Apple manages the encryption keys and could theoretically access the data. For apps that need end-to-end encryption regardless of the user’s ADP setting, wrap the CloudKit backend with EnsemblesEncrypted:  This encrypts data with AES-256-GCM before it ever reaches CloudKit, so security does not depend on Apple’s infrastructure. Custom Zones The two private-database initializers write to different CloudKit zones: init(ubiquityContainerIdentifier:rootDirectory:usePublicDatabase:schemaVersion:) writes to CloudKit’s default zone (_defaultZone). init(privateDatabaseForUbiquityContainerIdentifier:schemaVersion:) writes to a custom zone, com.mentalfaculty.ensembles.zone.schema2. This is the recommended choice for new apps because the custom zone supports efficient change tracking via CKServerChangeToken. When migrating an existing Ensembles 2 fleet, your E3 build must use the same initializer that your E2 build used. Devices in different zones cannot see each other’s records, even when pointing at the same iCloud container with the same schema version. See doc:MigratingFromEnsembles2 for details. Delegate Implement CloudKitFileSystemDelegate to customize CloudKit behavior, handle errors, and manage sharing:

rawIndexableTextContent: Unlike fileExists(atPath:), never answers from the listing cache: the server is asked in both directions. A cached “exists” can be stale in exactly the case this method exists to catch — a cloud reset behind a change token the server kept accepting — and answering the registration check from that cache would defeat the check. The result heals the cache either way: a hit is noted, and a miss removes any stale entry so later listings agree with the server.
